title: Translated Splahes & End Poem
description: A Simple Minecraft resource pack that translates the End Poem and splash texts into multiple languages, making hidden content accessible and emotionally meaningful across versions.
body:
**Translated Splashes & End Poem** is a resource pack that brings Minecraft’s most poetic and iconic texts to life in multiple languages, preserving their depth, humor, and emotional impact. It doesn’t alter graphics or gameplay—just the words that matter most.

---

# 📜 What’s Included?

## 🌌 1. The End Poem (end.txt)
The mysterious narration that appears after defeating the Ender Dragon, now beautifully localized. Each line has been carefully adapted to retain:
- The contemplative tone of the “beings of the void”
- Cosmic metaphors (“the long dream of life”)
- Technical nods (“lines of code on a screen”)

> “And the universe said: I love you because you are love.”


## 🎮 2. Title Screen Splashes (splashes.txt)
All those quirky, random messages on the main menu—now localized without losing their charm:
- Cultural references: “Technoblade never dies”
- Memes and jokes: “sqrt(-1) loves you”
- Technical winks: “Use LWJGL!”

> “Han shot first!” (Yes, the Star Wars reference is still intact)

---

# 🌐 Why This Pack Stands Out

- 🧠 Human-crafted translations – No machine translation. Every line is adapted by humans, for humans.
- 💫 Preserves Minecraft’s spirit – The poetry, humor, and quirks of Mojang’s writing remain intact.
- 🔄 Compatible with mods and other packs – Only modifies text files, leaving models and textures untouched.
- 🌎 Multilingual support – Perfect for international servers, global creators, and players who want Minecraft in their native language.

---

# 👥 Who’s It For?

- Casual players who want a richer experience in their own language
- Multilingual servers seeking consistent, meaningful text
- Content creators showcasing Minecraft across cultures

---

# 📦 Installation (Super Easy!)

1. Download the .zip file  
2. Drop it into your resourcepacks folder  
3. Activate it from Minecraft’s settings menu
